850:     /// ASGSL: Assignment inside a control-flow condition.
851:     fn check_inline_assignment(
852:         &self,
853:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
854:         results: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
855:     ) {
856:         if !self.is_check_enabled("ASGSL") {
857:             return;
858:         }
859: 
860:         // Walk ancestors to see if this assignment is inside a condition
861:         let mut current = node.parent();
862:         while let Some(parent) = current {
863:             match parent.kind() {
864:                 "if_statement" | "while_statement" | "for_statement" => {
865:                     // Check if the assignment is in the condition part
866:                     // (first child of if/while, second child of for)
867:                     results.push(self.diag(
868:                         "ASGSL",
869:                         "Avoid assignment inside control-flow condition; \
870:                          assign on a separate line for clarity",
871:                         node,
872:                         None,
873:                     ));
874:                     return;
875:                 }
876:                 "block" | "source_file" | "function_definition" => {
877:                     // Reached a block boundary — not in a condition
878:                     return;
879:                 }
880:                 _ => {
881:                     current = parent.parent();
882:                 }
883:             }
884:         }
885:     }
886: 
887:     /// NBRAK2: Unnecessary brackets `[x]` for scalar expression.
888:     fn check_unnecessary_brackets(
889:         &self,
890:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
891:         source: &str,
892:         results: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
893:     ) {
894:         if !self.is_check_enabled("NBRAK2") {
895:             return;
896:         }
897: 
898:         // A matrix node with exactly one named child that is a "row" with
899:         // exactly one element is `[scalar]`.
900:         let named_count = node.named_child_count();
901:         if named_count != 1 {
902:             return;
903:         }
904: 
905:         let row = match node.named_child(0) {
906:             Some(r) => r,
907:             None => return,
908:         };
909: 
910:         // The row should have exactly one named child (the scalar expression)
911:         if row.kind() == "row" && row.named_child_count() == 1 {
912:             if let Some(inner) = row.named_child(0) {
913:                 // Don't flag complex expressions or function calls that might
914:                 // rely on concatenation behavior
915:                 if matches!(inner.kind(), "identifier" | "number" | "string") {
916:                     let inner_text = &source[inner.start_byte()..inner.end_byte()];
917:                     results.push(self.diag(
918:                         "NBRAK2",
919:                         "Unnecessary brackets around scalar expression",
920:                         node,
921:                         Some(Fix::new(
922:                             node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
923:                             inner_text.to_string(),
924:                         )),
925:                     ));
926:                 }
927:             }
928:         }
929:     }
930: 
931:     /// RPMTT, RPMTF: Boolean tautologies `x | true` → `true`, `x & false` → `false`
932:     fn check_boolean_tautology(
933:         &self,
934:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
935:         source: &str,
936:         results: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
937:     ) {
938:         // Need at least: lhs, operator_token, rhs
939:         if node.child_count() < 3 {
940:             return;
941:         }
942: 
943:         // Extract the operator token (unnamed child between named children)
944:         let op_text = extract_operator_text(node, source);
945: 
946:         let (lhs, rhs) = match (node.named_child(0), node.named_child(1)) {
947:             (Some(l), Some(r)) => (l, r),
948:             _ => return,
949:         };
950: 
951:         let lhs_text = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
952:         let rhs_text = &source[rhs.start_byte()..rhs.end_byte()];
953: 
954:         // x | true → true  OR  true | x → true
955:         if (op_text == "|" || op_text == "||")
956:             && self.is_check_enabled("RPMTT")
957:             && (rhs_text == "true" || lhs_text == "true")
958:         {
959:             results.push(self.diag(
960:                 "RPMTT",
961:                 "Redundant boolean: 'x | true' is always 'true'",
962:                 node,
963:                 Some(Fix::new(node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(), "true")),
964:             ));
965:             return;
966:         }
967: 
968:         // x & false → false  OR  false & x → false
969:         if (op_text == "&" || op_text == "&&")
970:             && self.is_check_enabled("RPMTF")
971:             && (rhs_text == "false" || lhs_text == "false")
972:         {
973:             results.push(self.diag(
974:                 "RPMTF",
975:                 "Redundant boolean: 'x & false' is always 'false'",
976:                 node,
977:                 Some(Fix::new(node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(), "false")),
978:             ));
979:         }
980:     }
981: 
982:     /// RPMT1, RPMT0, RPMTI, RPMTN: Redundant arithmetic with constants
983:     fn check_redundant_arithmetic(
984:         &self,
985:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
986:         source: &str,
987:         results: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
988:     ) {
989:         if node.child_count() < 3 {
990:             return;
991:         }
992: 
993:         let op_text = extract_operator_text(node, source);
994: 
995:         let (lhs, rhs) = match (node.named_child(0), node.named_child(1)) {
996:             (Some(l), Some(r)) => (l, r),
997:             _ => return,
998:         };
999: 
1000:         let lhs_text = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
1001:         let rhs_text = &source[rhs.start_byte()..rhs.end_byte()];
1002: 
1003:         match op_text {
1004:             "*" | ".*" => {
1005:                 // RPMT1: x * 1 → x
1006:                 if self.is_check_enabled("RPMT1") && rhs_text == "1" {
1007:                     results.push(self.diag(
1008:                         "RPMT1",
1009:                         "Redundant multiplication by 1; simplify to 'x'",
1010:                         node,
1011:                         Some(Fix::new(
1012:                             node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1013:                             lhs_text.to_string(),
1014:                         )),
1015:                     ));
1016:                     return;
1017:                 }
1018:                 if self.is_check_enabled("RPMT1") && lhs_text == "1" {
1019:                     results.push(self.diag(
1020:                         "RPMT1",
1021:                         "Redundant multiplication by 1; simplify to 'x'",
1022:                         node,
1023:                         Some(Fix::new(
1024:                             node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1025:                             rhs_text.to_string(),
1026:                         )),
1027:                     ));
1028:                     return;
1029:                 }
1030: 
1031:                 // RPMT0: x * 0 → zeros(size(x))
1032:                 if self.is_check_enabled("RPMT0") && rhs_text == "0" {
1033:                     results.push(self.diag(
1034:                         "RPMT0",
1035:                         "Multiplication by 0; consider 'zeros(size(x))' for clarity",
1036:                         node,
1037:                         Some(Fix::new(
1038:                             node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1039:                             format!("zeros(size({lhs_text}))"),
1040:                         )),
1041:                     ));
1042:                 } else if self.is_check_enabled("RPMT0") && lhs_text == "0" {
1043:                     results.push(self.diag(
1044:                         "RPMT0",
1045:                         "Multiplication by 0; consider 'zeros(size(x))' for clarity",
1046:                         node,
1047:                         Some(Fix::new(
1048:                             node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1049:                             format!("zeros(size({rhs_text}))"),
1050:                         )),
1051:                     ));
1052:                 }
1053:             }
1054:             "+" => {
1055:                 // RPMTI: x + 0 → x
1056:                 if self.is_check_enabled("RPMTI") && rhs_text == "0" {
1057:                     results.push(self.diag(
1058:                         "RPMTI",
1059:                         "Redundant addition of 0; simplify to 'x'",
1060:                         node,
1061:                         Some(Fix::new(
1062:                             node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1063:                             lhs_text.to_string(),
1064:                         )),
1065:                     ));
1066:                 } else if self.is_check_enabled("RPMTI") && lhs_text == "0" {
1067:                     results.push(self.diag(
1068:                         "RPMTI",
1069:                         "Redundant addition of 0; simplify to 'x'",
1070:                         node,
1071:                         Some(Fix::new(
1072:                             node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1073:                             rhs_text.to_string(),
1074:                         )),
1075:                     ));
1076:                 }
1077:             }
1078:             "-" if self.is_check_enabled("RPMTN") && rhs_text == "0" => {
1079:                 // RPMTN: x - 0 → x
1080:                 results.push(self.diag(
1081:                     "RPMTN",
1082:                     "Redundant subtraction of 0; simplify to 'x'",
1083:                     node,
1084:                     Some(Fix::new(
1085:                         node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1086:                         lhs_text.to_string(),
1087:                     )),
1088:                 ));
1089:             }
1090:             _ => {}
1091:         }
1092:     }
1093: }

1099: impl Rule for ReadabilityEngine {
1100:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str {
1101:         "READABILITY_ENGINE"
1102:     }
1103: 
1104:     fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
1105:         "Readability improvement checks for MATLAB code"
1106:     }
1107: 
1108:     fn severity(&self) -> Severity {
1109:         Severity::Info
1110:     }
1111: 
1112:     fn category(&self) -> Category {
1113:         Category::Readability
1114:     }
1115: 
1116:     fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
1117:         TARGET_NODES
1118:     }
1119: 
1120:     fn check(&self, ctx: &NodeContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
1121:         let mut results = Vec::new();
1122: 
1123:         match ctx.node.kind() {
1124:             "function_call" => self.check_function_call(ctx, &mut results),
1125:             "comparison_operator" => self.check_comparison(ctx, &mut results),
1126:             "boolean_operator" => self.check_boolean_operator(ctx, &mut results),
1127:             "assignment" => self.check_assignment(ctx, &mut results),
1128:             "binary_operator" => self.check_binary_operator(ctx, &mut results),
1129:             "matrix" => self.check_matrix(ctx, &mut results),
1130:             // `identifier` nodes are handled via `assignment` LHS check (IJCL)
1131:             // rather than standalone identifier dispatch, to avoid false
1132:             // positives on identifier reads.
1133:             _ => {}
1134:         }
1135: 
1136:         results
1137:     }
1138: }

1141: // Helpers
1142: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1143: 
1144: /// Find the `arguments` child of a `function_call` node.
1145: ///
1146: /// In tree-sitter-matlab the call arguments are a child node of kind
1147: /// `arguments` rather than a named field, so `child_by_field_name("arguments")`
1148: /// never matches. This helper locates them by child kind instead.
1149: fn find_arguments(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> Option<tree_sitter::Node> {
1150:     node.named_children(&mut node.walk())
1151:         .find(|c| c.kind() == "arguments")
1152: }
1153: 
1154: /// Check if a string literal represents an empty string (`''` or `""`).
1155: fn is_empty_string(s: &str) -> bool {
1156:     s == "''" || s == "\"\""
1157: }
1158: 
1159: /// Check if a node is inside an `if_statement` condition.
1160: fn is_inside_if_condition(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
1161:     let mut current = node.parent();
1162:     while let Some(parent) = current {
1163:         match parent.kind() {
1164:             "if_statement" => return true,
1165:             "block" | "source_file" | "function_definition" => return false,
1166:             _ => current = parent.parent(),
1167:         }
1168:     }
1169:     false
1170: }
1171: 
1172: /// Extract the operator text from a binary/boolean operator node.
1173: ///
1174: /// Iterates over unnamed children to find the operator token between operands.
1175: fn extract_operator_text<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
1176:     // Walk all children (including unnamed) looking for the operator
1177:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
1178:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1179:         if !child.is_named() {
1180:             let text = &source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()];
1181:             // Operator tokens are things like +, -, *, .*, |, ||, &, &&, ==
1182:             if !text.trim().is_empty()
1183:                 && text != "("
1184:                 && text != ")"
1185:                 && text != "["
1186:                 && text != "]"
1187:             {
1188:                 return text;
1189:             }
1190:         }
1191:     }
1192:     ""
1193: }

1: //! # PERFORMANCE_ENGINE: Performance Improvement Checks
2: //!
3: //! A hybrid rule module implementing 41 performance-related MATLAB lint checks.
4: //! Most checks operate at the node level (function calls, operators, commands),
5: //! while AGROW, SAGROW, and PFBNS require file-level traversal to detect
6: //! array growth patterns inside loops.
7: //!
8: //! ## Architecture
9: //!
10: //! A single `PerformanceEngine` struct handles all 41 checks. Node-level checks
11: //! are dispatched by node kind (`function_call`, `command`, `binary_operator`,
12: //! `boolean_operator`, `comparison_operator`). File-level checks traverse the
13: //! full tree looking for growth patterns inside `for_statement`/`while_statement`.
14: //!
15: //! ## Examples
16: //!
17: //! Bad:
18: //! ```matlab
19: //! for i = 1:n
20: //!     x = [x, val];          % AGROW
21: //! end
22: //! if a & b                   % AND2
23: //! inv(A) * b                 % MINV
24: //! exist('foo', 'file')       % EXIST
25: //! ```
26: //!
27: //! Good:
28: //! ```matlab
29: //! x = zeros(1, n);

258:         // LAXES: gca/gcf calls (suggest caching)
259:         if self.is_enabled("LAXES") && (func_name == "gca" || func_name == "gcf") {
260:             diags.push(make_diag("LAXES", node));
261:         }
262: 
263:         // MRPBW: im2bw
264:         if self.is_enabled("MRPBW") && func_name == "im2bw" {
265:             diags.push(make_diag_with_fix(
266:                 "MRPBW",
267:                 node,
268:                 Some(fix_rename_func(node, source, "imbinarize")),
269:             ));
270:         }
271: 
272:         // TRSRT: sort then index — detect sort() call inside subscript or
273:         // assigned then immediately indexed. Simplified: flag sort() when
274:         // used as a subscript argument.
275:         if self.is_enabled("TRSRT") && func_name == "sort" && is_subscript_context(node) {
276:             diags.push(make_diag("TRSRT", node));
277:         }
278: 
279:         // RGXPI: regexp/regexpi with 'ignorecase' option
280:         if self.is_enabled("RGXPI")
281:             && func_name == "regexp"
282:             && has_string_arg(node, source, "ignorecase")
283:         {
284:             diags.push(make_diag("RGXPI", node));
285:         }
286: 
287:         // RGXP1: regexp/regexpi with overly simple patterns
288:         if self.is_enabled("RGXP1")
289:             && (func_name == "regexp" || func_name == "regexpi")
290:             && has_simple_regex_pattern(node, source)
291:         {
292:             diags.push(make_diag("RGXP1", node));
293:         }
294: 
295:         // TRIM1: deblank → strtrim
296:         if self.is_enabled("TRIM1") && func_name == "deblank" {
297:             diags.push(make_diag_with_fix(
298:                 "TRIM1",
299:                 node,
300:                 Some(fix_rename_func(node, source, "strtrim")),
301:             ));
302:         }
303: 
304:         // TRIM2: strtrim → strip
305:         if self.is_enabled("TRIM2") && func_name == "strtrim" {
306:             diags.push(make_diag_with_fix(
307:                 "TRIM2",
308:                 node,
309:                 Some(fix_rename_func(node, source, "strip")),
310:             ));
311:         }
312: 
313:         // STTOK: strtok inside loop
314:         if self.is_enabled("STTOK") && func_name == "strtok" && is_inside_loop(node) {
315:             diags.push(make_diag("STTOK", node));
316:         }
317: 
318:         // FNDSB: findstr
319:         if self.is_enabled("FNDSB") && func_name == "findstr" {
320:             diags.push(make_diag_with_fix(
321:                 "FNDSB",
322:                 node,
323:                 Some(fix_rename_func(node, source, "contains")),
324:             ));
325:         }
326: 
327:         // SPRIX: sparse indexing with logical — detect sparse() inside subscript
328:         if self.is_enabled("SPRIX") && func_name == "sparse" && is_subscript_context(node) {
329:             diags.push(make_diag("SPRIX", node));
330:         }
331: 
332:         // GRIDD: repmat for grid generation
333:         if self.is_enabled("GRIDD") && func_name == "repmat" {
334:             diags.push(make_diag("GRIDD", node));
335:         }
336: 
337:         // STNCI: lower(strcmp(...)) or upper(strcmp(...)) pattern
338:         if self.is_enabled("STNCI")
339:             && (func_name == "lower" || func_name == "upper")
340:             && has_strcmp_arg(node, source)
341:         {
342:             diags.push(make_diag("STNCI", node));
343:         }
344: 
345:         // STCCS: ~isempty(strfind(...)) → contains
346:         // This requires checking unary_operator parent, handled in check_unary
347: 
348:         diags
349:     }

351:     /// Check a `command` node for clear-related patterns.
352:     fn check_command<'a>(
353:         &self,
354:         node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>,
355:         source: &'a str,
356:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
357:         let mut diags = Vec::new();
358: 
359:         let cmd_name = match extract_command_name(node, source) {
360:             Some(n) => n,
361:             None => return diags,
362:         };
363: 
364:         if cmd_name != "clear" {
365:             return diags;
366:         }
367: 
368:         let args = extract_command_args(node, source);
369: 
370:         // CLEAR0ARGS: clear with no arguments
371:         if self.is_enabled("CLEAR0ARGS") && args.is_empty() {
372:             diags.push(make_diag("CLEAR0ARGS", node));
373:         }
374: 
375:         // CLALL: clear all
376:         if self.is_enabled("CLALL") && args.contains(&"all") {
377:             diags.push(make_diag("CLALL", node));
378:         }
379: 
380:         // CLCLS: clear classes
381:         if self.is_enabled("CLCLS") && args.contains(&"classes") {
382:             diags.push(make_diag("CLCLS", node));
383:         }
384: 
385:         // CLFUNC: clear functions
386:         if self.is_enabled("CLFUNC") && args.contains(&"functions") {
387:             diags.push(make_diag("CLFUNC", node));
388:         }
389: 
390:         // CLJAVA: clear java
391:         if self.is_enabled("CLJAVA") && args.contains(&"java") {
392:             diags.push(make_diag("CLJAVA", node));
393:         }
394: 
395:         // CLMEX: clear mex
396:         if self.is_enabled("CLMEX") && args.contains(&"mex") {
397:             diags.push(make_diag("CLMEX", node));
398:         }
399: 
400:         diags
401:     }

403:     /// Check `binary_operator` for MINV and MMTC patterns.
404:     fn check_binary_operator<'a>(
405:         &self,
406:         node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>,
407:         source: &'a str,
408:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
409:         let mut diags = Vec::new();
410:         let op = extract_operator(node, source);
411: 
412:         // MINV: inv(A) * b or b * inv(A)
413:         if self.is_enabled("MINV") && op == "*"
414:             && has_inv_operand(node, source) {
415:                 diags.push(make_diag("MINV", node));
416:             }
417: 
418:         // MMTC: x .* x → x.^2
419:         if self.is_enabled("MMTC") && op == ".*"
420:             && has_same_operands(node, source) {
421:                 diags.push(make_diag("MMTC", node));
422:             }
423: 
424:         diags
425:     }

427:     /// Check `boolean_operator` for AND2/OR2 patterns.
428:     ///
429:     /// In tree-sitter-matlab, `&&` and `||` parse as `boolean_operator`, while
430:     /// `&` and `|` parse as `binary_operator`. This check fires on
431:     /// `binary_operator` nodes with `&` or `|` that are inside boolean
432:     /// contexts (if/while conditions).
433:     fn check_boolean_context_binary<'a>(
434:         &self,
435:         node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>,
436:         source: &'a str,
437:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
438:         let mut diags = Vec::new();
439:         let op = extract_operator(node, source);
440: 
441:         // AND2: & in boolean context
442:         if self.is_enabled("AND2") && op == "&" && is_in_condition(node) {
443:             diags.push(make_diag_with_fix(
444:                 "AND2",
445:                 node,
446:                 fix_replace_operator(node, source, "&", "&&"),
447:             ));
448:         }
449: 
450:         // OR2: | in boolean context
451:         if self.is_enabled("OR2") && op == "|" && is_in_condition(node) {
452:             diags.push(make_diag_with_fix(
453:                 "OR2",
454:                 node,
455:                 fix_replace_operator(node, source, "|", "||"),
456:             ));
457:         }
458: 
459:         diags
460:     }

462:     /// Check `comparison_operator` for ISMT/ISCL patterns.
463:     fn check_comparison<'a>(
464:         &self,
465:         node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>,
466:         source: &'a str,
467:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
468:         let mut diags = Vec::new();
469: 
470:         // Pattern: length(x) == 0 → isempty(x)
471:         // Pattern: length(x) == 1 → isscalar(x)
472:         if let Some((func, val)) = extract_length_comparison(node, source) {
473:             if func == "length" {
474:                 if self.is_enabled("ISMT") && val == "0" {
475:                     diags.push(make_diag("ISMT", node));
476:                 }
477:                 if self.is_enabled("ISCL") && val == "1" {
478:                     diags.push(make_diag("ISCL", node));
479:                 }
480:             }
481:         }
482: 
483:         diags
484:     }

486:     /// Check `unary_operator` for STCCS pattern: ~isempty(strfind(...))
487:     fn check_unary<'a>(
488:         &self,
489:         node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>,
490:         source: &'a str,
491:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
492:         let mut diags = Vec::new();
493: 
494:         if !self.is_enabled("STCCS") {
495:             return diags;
496:         }
497: 
498:         // Pattern: ~isempty(strfind(...))
499:         let op = extract_unary_operator(node, source);
500:         if op != "~" {
501:             return diags;
502:         }
503: 
504:         // The operand should be a function_call to isempty
505:         let operand = match node.child(1).or_else(|| node.child_by_field_name("operand")) {
506:             Some(n) => n,
507:             None => return diags,
508:         };
509: 
510:         if operand.kind() == "function_call" {
511:             if let Some(name) = extract_func_name(operand, source) {
512:                 if name == "isempty" {
513:                     // Check if the argument to isempty is strfind(...)
514:                     if let Some(args_node) = find_arguments(operand) {
515:                         if let Some(first_arg) = first_named_child(args_node) {
516:                             if first_arg.kind() == "function_call" {
517:                                 if let Some(inner_name) = extract_func_name(first_arg, source) {
518:                                     if inner_name == "strfind" {
519:                                         diags.push(make_diag("STCCS", node));
520:                                     }
521:                                 }
522:                             }
523:                         }
524:                     }
525:                 }
526:             }
527:         }
528: 
529:         diags
530:     }

533:     // File-level checks: AGROW, SAGROW, PFBNS

536:     /// File-level check for array/struct growth inside loops.
537:     fn check_growth_in_loops(
538:         &self,
539:         tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
540:         source: &str,
541:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
542:         let mut diags = Vec::new();
543:         let root = tree.root_node();
544:         self.traverse_for_growth(&root, source, false, &mut diags);
545:         diags
546:     }
547: 
548:     /// Recursive traversal looking for growth patterns inside loops.
549:     fn traverse_for_growth(
550:         &self,
551:         node: &tree_sitter::Node,
552:         source: &str,
553:         in_loop: bool,
554:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
555:     ) {
556:         let kind = node.kind();
557:         let entering_loop = kind == "for_statement" || kind == "while_statement";
558:         let now_in_loop = in_loop || entering_loop;
559: 
560:         // Only check assignment nodes inside loops.
561:         if now_in_loop && kind == "assignment" {
562:             self.check_assignment_growth(*node, source, diags);
563:         }
564: 
565:         // Also detect growth via full-node text for assignments that tree-sitter
566:         // may parse differently (e.g., s.field(end+1) = k might parse as
567:         // a function_call at statement level rather than an assignment).
568:         if now_in_loop
569:             && (kind == "function_call" || kind == "cell_index")
570:             && is_statement_level(node)
571:         {
572:             let text = node_text(*node, source);
573:             let normalized: String = text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
574:             if normalized.contains("end+1") {
575:                 let has_dot = text.contains('.');
576:                 let check_id = if has_dot { "SAGROW" } else { "AGROW" };
577:                 if self.is_enabled(check_id) {
578:                     diags.push(make_diag(check_id, *node));
579:                 }
580:             }
581:         }
582: 
583:         let count = node.child_count();
584:         for i in 0..count {
585:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
586:                 self.traverse_for_growth(&child, source, now_in_loop, diags);
587:             }
588:         }
589:     }
590: 
591:     /// Check a single assignment node for growth patterns.
592:     ///
593:     /// Detects:
594:     /// 1. `x = [x, val]` or `x = [x; val]` — concatenation growth (AGROW)
595:     /// 2. `x(end+1) = val` — end+1 indexing (AGROW)
596:     /// 3. `x{end+1} = val` — cell growth (AGROW)
597:     /// 4. `s.field(end+1) = val` — struct field growth (SAGROW)
598:     /// 5. `x = []` followed by growth — PFBNS (simplified: flag end+1 patterns)
599:     fn check_assignment_growth(
600:         &self,
601:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
602:         source: &str,
603:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
604:     ) {
605:         let lhs = match node.child_by_field_name("left").or_else(|| node.child(0)) {
606:             Some(n) => n,
607:             None => return,
608:         };
609:         let rhs = match node.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| node.child(2)) {
610:             Some(n) => n,
611:             None => return,
612:         };
613: 
614:         let lhs_text = node_text(lhs, source);
615:         let rhs_text = node_text(rhs, source);
616: 
617:         // Determine if LHS involves a struct field (for SAGROW vs AGROW).
618:         let is_struct = lhs.kind() == "field_expression"
619:             || (lhs.kind() == "function_call" && lhs_text.contains('.'));
620: 
621:         let check_id = if is_struct { "SAGROW" } else { "AGROW" };
622: 
623:         if !self.is_enabled(check_id) {
624:             return;
625:         }
626: 
627:         // Pattern 1: x(end+1) = ... or x{end+1} = ...
628:         // LHS is a function_call (indexing) or cell_index containing "end+1"
629:         // or "end + 1".
630:         if (lhs.kind() == "function_call" || lhs.kind() == "cell_index")
631:             && contains_end_plus_pattern(lhs, source)
632:         {
633:             diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
634:             return;
635:         }
636: 
637:         // Pattern 1b: s.field(end+1) = ... — may parse with field_expression as LHS
638:         // and end+1 in the assignment text before the `=`.
639:         if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
640:             // Check the full assignment text up to the `=` for end+1 pattern.
641:             let assign_text = node_text(node, source);
642:             if let Some(eq_pos) = assign_text.find('=') {
643:                 let lhs_full = &assign_text[..eq_pos];
644:                 let normalized: String = lhs_full.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
645:                 if normalized.contains("end+1") {
646:                     diags.push(make_diag("SAGROW", node));
647:                     return;
648:                 }
649:             }
650:         }
651: 
652:         // Pattern 2: x = [x, val] or x = [x; val]
653:         // LHS is a simple identifier, RHS is a matrix containing that identifier.
654:         if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
655:             let var_name = lhs_text;
656:             if rhs.kind() == "matrix" && matrix_contains_var(rhs, source, var_name) {
657:                 diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
658:                 return;
659:             }
660:             // Also check cell: x = {x, val} — though less common
661:             if rhs.kind() == "cell" && matrix_contains_var(rhs, source, var_name) {
662:                 diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
663:                 return;
664:             }
665:         }
666: 
667:         // Pattern 3: s.field = [s.field, val]
668:         if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
669:             let field_text = lhs_text;
670:             if rhs.kind() == "matrix" && rhs_text.contains(field_text) {
671:                 diags.push(make_diag("SAGROW", node));
672:             }
673:         }
674:     }
675: }

677: impl Rule for PerformanceEngine {
678:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str {
679:         "PERFORMANCE_ENGINE"
680:     }
681: 
682:     fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
683:         "Performance improvement suggestions"
684:     }
685: 
686:     fn severity(&self) -> Severity {
687:         Severity::Info
688:     }
689: 
690:     fn category(&self) -> Category {
691:         Category::Performance
692:     }
693: 
694:     fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
695:         TARGET_NODES
696:     }
697: 
698:     fn has_file_check(&self) -> bool {
699:         true
700:     }
701: 
702:     fn check(&self, ctx: &NodeContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
703:         match ctx.node.kind() {
704:             "function_call" => self.check_function_call(ctx.node, ctx.source),
705:             "command" => self.check_command(ctx.node, ctx.source),
706:             "binary_operator" => {
707:                 let mut diags = self.check_binary_operator(ctx.node, ctx.source);
708:                 // Also check for AND2/OR2 (& and | parse as binary_operator).
709:                 diags.extend(self.check_boolean_context_binary(ctx.node, ctx.source));
710:                 diags
711:             }
712:             "boolean_operator" => {
713:                 // boolean_operator is for && / || which are already correct.
714:                 Vec::new()
715:             }
716:             "comparison_operator" => self.check_comparison(ctx.node, ctx.source),
717:             "unary_operator" => self.check_unary(ctx.node, ctx.source),
718:             _ => Vec::new(),
719:         }
720:     }
721: 
722:     fn check_file(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
723:         self.check_growth_in_loops(ctx.tree, ctx.source)
724:     }
725: }

731: /// Build a diagnostic from a check ID and node.
732: fn make_diag(check_id: &'static str, node: tree_sitter::Node) -> Diagnostic {
733:     let start = node.start_position();
734:     Diagnostic {
735:         rule_id: check_id,
736:         message: check_description(check_id).to_string(),
737:         severity: Severity::Info,
738:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
739:         line: start.row + 1,
740:         column: start.column + 1,
741:         fix: None,
742:     }
743: }

746: fn make_diag_with_fix(
747:     check_id: &'static str,
748:     node: tree_sitter::Node,
749:     fix: Option<Fix>,
750: ) -> Diagnostic {

763: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
764: // Helper: node text extraction
765: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
766: 
767: /// Extract the raw text of a node.
768: fn node_text<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
769:     &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
770: }
771: 
772: /// Extract function name from a `function_call` node.
773: fn extract_func_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
774:     if node.kind() != "function_call" {
775:         return None;
776:     }
777:     let name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
778:     Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
779: }
780: 
781: /// Extract command name from a `command` node.
782: fn extract_command_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
783:     if node.kind() != "command" {
784:         return None;
785:     }
786:     let name_node = node.child(0)?;
787:     if name_node.kind() == "command_name" {
788:         Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
789:     } else {
790:         None
791:     }
792: }
793: 
794: /// Extract command arguments as a list of text fragments.
795: fn extract_command_args<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Vec<&'a str> {
796:     let mut args = Vec::new();
797:     let count = node.child_count();
798:     for i in 0..count {
799:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
800:             // Skip the command_name (first child) and punctuation.
801:             if child.kind() == "command_name" || child.kind() == ";" || child.kind() == "," {
802:                 continue;
803:             }
804:             let text = node_text(child, source).trim();
805:             if !text.is_empty() {
806:                 args.push(text);
807:             }
808:         }
809:     }
810:     args
811: }
812: 
813: /// Extract the operator text from a `binary_operator` or `boolean_operator`.
814: fn extract_operator<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
815:     // The operator is typically the second child (between left and right operands),
816:     // or we can scan children for the operator token.
817:     let count = node.child_count();
818:     for i in 0..count {
819:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
820:             let text = node_text(child, source);
821:             // Operator tokens are short and not identifiers/expressions.
822:             match text {
823:                 "+" | "-" | "*" | "/" | "\\" | "^" | ".*" | "./" | ".\\" | ".^" | "&" | "|"
824:                 | "&&" | "||" | "==" | "~=" | "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">=" => return text,
825:                 _ => continue,
826:             }
827:         }
828:     }
829:     ""
830: }
831: 
832: /// Extract the operator text from a `unary_operator` node.
833: fn extract_unary_operator<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
834:     if let Some(child) = node.child(0) {
835:         let text = node_text(child, source);
836:         match text {
837:             "~" | "-" | "+" | "!" => return text,
838:             _ => {}
839:         }
840:     }
841:     ""
842: }
843: 
844: /// Get the first named child of a node.
845: fn first_named_child(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> Option<tree_sitter::Node> {
846:     let count = node.named_child_count();
847:     if count > 0 {
848:         node.named_child(0)
849:     } else {
850:         None
851:     }
852: }

854: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
855: // Helper: argument analysis
856: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
857: 
858: /// Count the number of arguments in a `function_call` node.
859: fn count_args(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> usize {
860:     // Arguments are in the `arguments` child node.
861:     match find_arguments(node) {
862:         Some(args_node) => args_node.named_child_count(),
863:         None => 0,
864:     }

618:     /// COMNC: Comment lacks space after `%`.

641:             severity: Severity::Info,

643:             line: pos.row + 1,
644:             column: pos.column + 1,
645:             fix: Some(mlt_core::Fix::new(

666:     /// LOGPROD / LOGMIN / LOGMAX: Using `prod`/`min`/`max` on logical values.
667:     fn check_logical_aggregation(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
668:         if node.kind() != "function_call" {
669:             return Vec::new();
670:         }
671: 
672:         let func_name = match get_function_call_name(node, source) {
673:             Some(n) => n,
674:             None => return Vec::new(),
675:         };
676: 
677:         let (check_id, replacement) = match func_name {
678:             "prod" if self.is_check_enabled("LOGPROD") => ("LOGPROD", "all"),
679:             "min" if self.is_check_enabled("LOGMIN") => ("LOGMIN", "all"),
680:             "max" if self.is_check_enabled("LOGMAX") => ("LOGMAX", "any"),
681:             _ => return Vec::new(),
682:         };
683: 
684:         // Heuristic: check if the argument is likely logical (named with `is`, `has`,
685:         // or is a comparison result). We can't know types statically, so this is
686:         // limited to obvious patterns.
687:         let args_node = find_child_of_kind(node, "arguments");
688:         let first_arg = args_node.and_then(|a| first_named_child(a));
689:         let looks_logical = first_arg
690:             .map(|arg| {
691:                 let kind = arg.kind();
692:                 if kind == "comparison_operator" || kind == "boolean_operator" {
693:                     return true;
694:                 }
695:                 if kind == "identifier" {
696:                     let name = node_text(arg, source);
697:                     return name.starts_with("is")
698:                         || name.starts_with("has")
699:                         || name == "true"
700:                         || name == "false";
701:                 }
702:                 if kind == "unary_operator" {
703:                     let text = node_text(arg, source);
704:                     return text.starts_with('~');
705:                 }
706:                 false
707:             })
708:             .unwrap_or(false);
709: 
710:         if !looks_logical {
711:             return Vec::new();
712:         }
713: 
714:         let pos = node.start_position();
715:         vec![Diagnostic {
716:             rule_id: check_id,
717:             message: format!(
718:                 "Use {replacement}() instead of {func_name}() for logical arrays"
719:             ),
720:             severity: Severity::Warning,
721:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
722:             line: pos.row + 1,
723:             column: pos.column + 1,
724:             fix: None,
725:         }]
726:     }

728:     /// SHOCIRAA: Short-circuit operator (`&&`/`||`) used where element-wise is expected.
729:     fn check_shociraa(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
730:         if !self.is_check_enabled("SHOCIRAA") || node.kind() != "boolean_operator" {

762:     /// UNRPWR: Power of negative base may produce complex result.
763:     fn check_unrpwr(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
764:         if !self.is_check_enabled("UNRPWR") || node.kind() != "binary_operator" {

768:         let text = node_text(node, source);

770:             return Vec::new();

773:         // Check if the left operand is a negative literal or unary negation.
774:         let left = node.child_by_field_name("left").or_else(|| node.child(0));

776:             .map(|l| {
777:                 if l.kind() == "unary_operator" {

795:             rule_id: "UNRPWR",

799:             line: pos.row + 1,

966:     /// WLAST: `warning` is the last statement in a function (may need `error` instead).
967:     fn check_wlast(&self, tree: &tree_sitter::Tree, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
968:         if !self.is_check_enabled("WLAST") {
969:             return Vec::new();
970:         }
971: 
972:         let meta = FileMeta::build(tree, source);
973:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
974: 
975:         for func in &meta.functions {
976:             self.check_wlast_in_range(tree.root_node(), source, func.byte_range.clone(), &mut diagnostics);
977:         }
978:         for func in &meta.local_functions {
979:             self.check_wlast_in_range(tree.root_node(), source, func.byte_range.clone(), &mut diagnostics);
980:         }
981: 
982:         diagnostics
983:     }

985:     /// Helper: check if the last statement in a byte range is a `warning()` call.
986:     fn check_wlast_in_range(
987:         &self,
988:         root: Node,
989:         source: &str,
990:         range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
991:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
992:     ) {
993:         // Find the function_definition node covering this range.
994:         let func_node = find_node_in_range(root, &range);
995:         let func_node = match func_node {
996:             Some(n) if n.kind() == "function_definition" => n,
997:             _ => return,
998:         };
999: 
1000:         // Get the block child (function body).
1001:         let block = match find_child_of_kind(func_node, "block") {
1002:             Some(b) => b,
1003:             None => return,
1004:         };
1005: 
1006:         // Find the last named non-`end` child.
1007:         let last_stmt = last_named_child_not_end(block);
1008:         let last_stmt = match last_stmt {
1009:             Some(s) => s,
1010:             None => return,
1011:         };
1012: 
1013:         // Check if it's a warning() call.
1014:         if last_stmt.kind() != "function_call" {
1015:             return;
1016:         }
1017:         let name = get_function_call_name(last_stmt, source);
1018:         if name != Some("warning") {
1019:             return;
1020:         }
1021: 
1022:         let pos = last_stmt.start_position();
1023:         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1024:             rule_id: "WLAST",
1025:             message: "warning() is the last statement in this function; did you mean error()?"
1026:                 .to_string(),
1027:             severity: Severity::Warning,
1028:             byte_range: last_stmt.start_byte()..last_stmt.end_byte(),
1029:             line: pos.row + 1,
1030:             column: pos.column + 1,
1031:             fix: None,
1032:         });
1033:     }

1175:     /// ITERS: Loop variable shadows an outer variable.
1176:     fn check_iters(&self, tree: &tree_sitter::Tree, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
1177:         if !self.is_check_enabled("ITERS") {
1178:             return Vec::new();
1179:         }
1180: 
1181:         let sym = SymbolTable::build(tree, source);
1182:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
1183: 
1184:         for (idx, scope) in sym.scopes.iter().enumerate() {
1185:             // For each for-iterator definition, check if the same name exists
1186:             // in a parent scope.
1187:             for def in &scope.defs {
1188:                 if def.kind != crate::analysis::symbols::DefKind::ForIterator {
1189:                     continue;
1190:                 }
1191:                 // Walk parent scopes.
1192:                 let mut parent_idx = scope.parent;
1193:                 while let Some(pidx) = parent_idx {
1194:                     let parent_scope = &sym.scopes[pidx];
1195:                     // Skip if it's the same scope index (shouldn't happen).
1196:                     if pidx == idx {
1197:                         break;
1198:                     }
1199:                     if parent_scope.is_defined(&def.name) {
1200:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1201:                             rule_id: "ITERS",
1202:                             message: format!(
1203:                                 "Loop variable '{}' shadows a variable in an outer scope",
1204:                                 def.name
1205:                             ),
1206:                             severity: Severity::Warning,
1207:                             byte_range: def.byte_range.clone(),
1208:                             line: def.line,
1209:                             column: def.column,
1210:                             fix: None,
1211:                         });
1212:                         break;
1213:                     }
1214:                     parent_idx = parent_scope.parent;
1215:                 }
1216:             }
1217:         }
1218: 
1219:         diagnostics
1220:     }

1774:         if child.kind() == "block" || child.kind() == "elseif_clause" || child.kind() == "else_clause" {
1775:             continue;
1776:         }
1777:         find_element_wise_boolean_in_condition(child, source, diagnostics);

1781: /// Find the function_definition node overlapping a byte range.
1782: fn find_node_in_range<'a>(root: Node<'a>, range: &std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Option<Node<'a>> {
1783:     if root.kind() == "function_definition"
1784:         && root.start_byte() == range.start
1785:         && root.end_byte() == range.end
1786:     {
1787:         return Some(root);
1788:     }
1789:     let mut cursor = root.walk();
1790:     for child in root.children(&mut cursor) {
1791:         if child.start_byte() > range.end || child.end_byte() < range.start {
1792:             continue;
1793:         }
1794:         if let Some(found) = find_node_in_range(child, range) {
1795:             return Some(found);
1796:         }
1797:     }
1798:     None
1799: }

1801: /// Collect statements grouped by line number (for SEPEX).
1802: fn collect_statements_by_line(
1803:     node: Node,
1804:     line_statements: &mut std::collections::HashMap<usize, Vec<(usize, usize)>>,
1805: ) {
1806:     let kind = node.kind();
1807: 
1808:     // Only collect at statement level in source_file or block.
1809:     if kind == "source_file" || kind == "block" {
1810:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
1811:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1812:             let ck = child.kind();
1813:             if ck == ";"
1814:                 || ck == ","
1815:                 || ck == "comment"
1816:                 || ck == "end"
1817:                 || ck == "line_continuation"
1818:                 || !child.is_named()
1819:             {
1820:                 continue;
1821:             }
1822:             let line = child.start_position().row + 1;
1823:             line_statements
1824:                 .entry(line)
1825:                 .or_default()
1826:                 .push((child.start_byte(), child.end_byte()));
1827:         }
1828:     }
1829: 
1830:     // Recurse into structural nodes.
1831:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
1832:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1833:         let ck = child.kind();
1834:         if ck == "block"
1835:             || ck == "function_definition"
1836:             || ck == "if_statement"
1837:             || ck == "for_statement"
1838:             || ck == "while_statement"
1839:             || ck == "switch_statement"
1840:             || ck == "try_statement"
1841:             || ck == "catch_clause"
1842:             || ck == "methods"
1843:             || ck == "class_definition"
1844:         {
1845:             collect_statements_by_line(child, line_statements);
1846:         }
1847:     }

1850: /// Find `end` used as an index argument (FNCOLND).
1851: fn find_end_as_index(node: Node, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
1852:     if node.kind() == "end" {
1853:         // Check if parent is an indexing context (function_call arguments).
1854:         if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
1855:             if parent.kind() == "arguments" {
1856:                 // Check if grandparent is a function_call (which could be indexing).
1857:                 if let Some(gp) = parent.parent() {
1858:                     if gp.kind() == "function_call" {
1859:                         // Count the number of argument separators (commas) to determine
1860:                         // if this is a multi-dimensional index. `end` without explicit
1861:                         // dimension is fine for 1-D indexing but ambiguous for multi-D.
1862:                         let comma_count = count_children_of_kind(parent, ",");
1863:                         if comma_count > 0 {
1864:                             let pos = node.start_position();
1865:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1866:                                 rule_id: "FNCOLND",
1867:                                 message: "'end' used in multi-dimensional indexing; specify the dimension explicitly".to_string(),
1868:                                 severity: Severity::Warning,
1869:                                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1870:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
1871:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
1872:                                 fix: None,
1873:                             });
1874:                         }
1875:                     }
1876:                 }
1877:             }
1878:         }
1879:     }
1880: 
1881:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
1882:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1883:         find_end_as_index(child, diagnostics);
1884:     }

1891:         .filter(|c| c.kind() == kind)
1892:         .count()

1: //! # Incomplete Analysis: Linter-Internal Limit Checks
2: //!
3: //! This module implements the 17 "Incomplete Analysis" checks from MATLAB's Code
4: //! Analyzer. These are special internal-limit diagnostics that **cannot be disabled**
5: //! by the user. They all have default severity `Error`.
6: //!
7: //! ## Check IDs
8: //!
9: //! | Check ID | Description                                  | Detection                                  |
10: //! |----------|----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
11: //! | TMMSG    | More than 10,000 diagnostics generated       | Post-lint (diagnostic count > threshold)   |
12: //! | TMSMS    | More than 1,000 parse errors generated       | Count ERROR nodes in tree                  |
13: //! | MXASET   | File too complex to analyze                  | Node count > threshold                     |
14: //! | QUIT     | Analysis did not complete                    | No-op (linter panic guard)                 |
15: //! | NOSPC    | File too complex (nesting)                   | Max nesting depth > threshold              |
16: //! | MBIG     | File too large                               | Source length > threshold                  |
17: //! | NOFIL    | File not found                               | No-op (handled by CLI)                     |
18: //! | MDOTM    | Invalid file extension                       | File extension != `.m`                     |
19: //! | MDMCR    | Deployed MATLAB file                         | File extension == `.ctf` or `.p`           |
20: //! | RDERR    | Unable to read file                          | No-op (handled by CLI)                     |
21: //! | EOFER    | Too many syntax errors                       | ERROR node count > threshold               |
22: //! | EOFMI    | Incomplete file                              | Last node is ERROR or MISSING              |
23: //! | MDEEP    | Parentheses/brackets nested too deeply       | Max `()`, `[]`, `{}` nesting depth         |
24: //! | DEEPC    | Block comments nested too deeply             | Nested `%{ %}` detection                   |
25: //! | DEEPN    | Functions nested too deeply                  | Nested `function_definition` depth         |
26: //! | DEEPS    | Statements nested too deeply                 | Nested if/for/while/switch/try depth       |
27: //! | TEXTL    | Text too long                                | Max line length > threshold                |
28: //!
29: //! ## Configuration
30: //!
31: //! ```toml
32: //! [lint.rules.INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS]
33: //! max_diagnostics = 10000
34: //! max_parse_errors = 1000
35: //! max_node_count = 100000
36: //! max_file_size = 1048576
37: //! max_paren_depth = 32
38: //! max_function_depth = 20
39: //! max_statement_depth = 15
40: //! max_line_length = 4096
41: //! ```

158: /// Incomplete Analysis Engine: a file-level rule that handles all 17
159: /// incomplete-analysis checks in a single pass.

161: /// These checks represent linter-internal limits and cannot be disabled
162: /// by the user (`can_be_disabled() == false`).
163: pub struct IncompleteAnalysisEngine {

167: impl IncompleteAnalysisEngine {
168:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
169:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
170:         let rule_config: IncompleteAnalysisConfig = config.rule_params("INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS");
171:         Box::new(Self {
172:             config: rule_config,
173:         })
174:     }

176:     /// Walk the tree and collect all metrics in one pass.
177:     fn collect_metrics(&self, root: Node) -> TreeMetrics {
178:         let mut metrics = TreeMetrics::default();
179: 
180:         // Check last child of root for EOFMI.
181:         if let Some(last) = last_descendant(root) {
182:             metrics.last_node_is_error = last.is_error() || last.is_missing();
183:         }

185:         Self::walk_tree(root, &mut metrics, 0, 0, 0);
186:         metrics
187:     }

189:     /// Recursive DFS traversal that collects node counts, error counts, and
190:     /// nesting depths in a single pass.
191:     fn walk_tree(
192:         node: Node,
193:         metrics: &mut TreeMetrics,
194:         paren_depth: usize,
195:         function_depth: usize,
196:         statement_depth: usize,
197:     ) {
198:         metrics.node_count += 1;
199: 
200:         if node.is_error() {
201:             metrics.error_count += 1;
202:         }
203: 
204:         // Track parentheses/bracket nesting depth (MDEEP).
205:         let new_paren_depth = match node.kind() {
206:             "parenthesis" | "arguments" | "matrix" | "cell" => {
207:                 let d = paren_depth + 1;
208:                 if d > metrics.max_paren_depth {
209:                     metrics.max_paren_depth = d;
210:                 }
211:                 d
212:             }
213:             _ => paren_depth,
214:         };
215: 
216:         // Track function nesting depth (DEEPN).
217:         let new_function_depth = if node.kind() == "function_definition" {
218:             let d = function_depth + 1;
219:             if d > metrics.max_function_depth {
220:                 metrics.max_function_depth = d;
221:             }
222:             d
223:         } else {
224:             function_depth
225:         };
226: 
227:         // Track statement nesting depth (DEEPS).
228:         let new_statement_depth = match node.kind() {
229:             "if_statement" | "for_statement" | "while_statement" | "switch_statement"
230:             | "try_statement" => {
231:                 let d = statement_depth + 1;
232:                 if d > metrics.max_statement_depth {
233:                     metrics.max_statement_depth = d;
234:                 }
235:                 d
236:             }
237:             _ => statement_depth,
238:         };
239: 
240:         // Recurse into children.
241:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
242:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
243:             Self::walk_tree(
244:                 child,
245:                 metrics,
246:                 new_paren_depth,

248:                 new_statement_depth,

256:         let mut byte_offset = 0;

269:                     line: line_idx + 1,
270:                     column: 1,
271:                     fix: None,
272:                 });
273:             }

275:             byte_offset += line.len() + 1;
276:         }

278:         diagnostics
279:     }

281:     /// Scan source text for nested block comments (DEEPC).
282:     ///
283:     /// MATLAB block comments are `%{ ... %}`. Nesting is not allowed — a
284:     /// second `%{` inside an open block comment is an error.
285:     fn check_nested_block_comments(&self, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
286:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
287:         let mut depth: usize = 0;
288:         let mut byte_offset = 0;
289: 
290:         for (line_idx, line) in source.lines().enumerate() {
291:             let trimmed = line.trim();
292:             if trimmed == "%{" {
293:                 depth += 1;
294:                 if depth > 1 {
295:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
296:                         rule_id: "DEEPC",
297:                         message: format!(
298:                             "Block comments nested too deeply (depth {depth})"
299:                         ),
300:                         severity: Severity::Error,
301:                         byte_range: byte_offset..byte_offset + line.len(),
302:                         line: line_idx + 1,
303:                         column: 1,
304:                         fix: None,
305:                     });
306:                 }
307:             } else if trimmed == "%}" {
308:                 depth = depth.saturating_sub(1);
309:             }
310:             byte_offset += line.len() + 1;
311:         }
312: 
313:         diagnostics
314:     }
315: }

381:     /// Heuristic: does this error look like a missing `end`?
382:     fn looks_like_missing_end(text: &str, node: &Node) -> bool {
383:         // If the error node is preceded by block-opening keywords.
384:         let block_openers = [
385:             "if", "for", "while", "switch", "try", "function", "classdef",
386:             "properties", "methods", "events", "enumeration",
387:         ];
388:         // Check text for block openers without matching end.
389:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
390:         let has_opener = block_openers.iter().any(|kw| lower.contains(kw));

393:         if has_opener && !has_end {

395:         }

397:         // Check if previous sibling is a block statement.
398:         if let Some(prev) = node.prev_sibling() {
399:             let kind = prev.kind();
400:             if block_openers.contains(&kind) {

402:             }
403:         }
404: 
405:         false

531:                 rule_id: "SOFOC",
532:                 message:
533:                     "Statements outside class definition in a class file are not allowed"
534:                         .to_string(),
535:                 severity: Severity::Error,
536:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
537:                 line: 1,
538:                 column: 1,
539:                 fix: None,
540:             });
541:         }
542: 
543:         // SEMFU: File has only empty statements (only `;` and whitespace).
544:         if self.is_check_enabled("SEMFU")
545:             && !has_any_real_content
546:             && class_count == 0
547:             && !source.trim().is_empty()
548:         {
549:             // Verify the file truly only has semicolons, whitespace, and comments.
550:             let only_empty = source
551:                 .lines()
552:                 .all(|line| {
553:                     let trimmed = line.trim();
554:                     trimmed.is_empty()
555:                         || trimmed == ";"
556:                         || trimmed.starts_with('%')
557:                 });
558:             if only_empty {
559:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
560:                     rule_id: "SEMFU",
561:                     message: "File contains only empty statements (semicolons and whitespace)"
562:                         .to_string(),
563:                     severity: Severity::Error,
564:                     byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
565:                     line: 1,
566:                     column: 1,
567:                     fix: None,
568:                 });
569:             }
570:         }
571: 
572:         diagnostics
573:     }

575:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
576:     // Function name validation (FNDOT, FNSWA)
577:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
578: 
579:     /// Check function names for issues (FNDOT, FNSWA).
580:     fn check_function_names(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
581:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
582:         self.walk_function_names(root, source, &mut diagnostics, false);
583:         diagnostics
584:     }
585: 
586:     /// Recursively walk to find function_definition nodes and validate names.
587:     fn walk_function_names(
588:         &self,
589:         node: Node,
590:         source: &str,
591:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
592:         in_methods_block: bool,
593:     ) {
594:         let kind = node.kind();
595:         let is_methods = kind == "methods";
596: 
597:         if kind == "function_definition" {
598:             // Find the function name node.
599:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
600:                 let name = &source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()];
601:                 let pos = name_node.start_position();
602: 
603:                 // FNSWA: Function name doesn't start with alphabetic character.
604:                 if self.is_check_enabled("FNSWA")
605:                     && !name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
606:                 {
607:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
608:                         rule_id: "FNSWA",
609:                         message: format!(
610:                             "Function name '{}' must start with an alphabetic character",
611:                             name
612:                         ),
613:                         severity: Severity::Error,
614:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
615:                         line: pos.row + 1,
616:                         column: pos.column + 1,
617:                         fix: None,
618:                     });
619:                 }
620: 
621:                 // FNDOT: Function name contains dots but is not in a class methods block.
622:                 if self.is_check_enabled("FNDOT") && name.contains('.') && !in_methods_block {
623:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
624:                         rule_id: "FNDOT",
625:                         message: format!(
626:                             "Function name '{}' contains dots but is not in a class methods block",
627:                             name
628:                         ),
629:                         severity: Severity::Error,
630:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
631:                         line: pos.row + 1,
632:                         column: pos.column + 1,
633:                         fix: None,
634:                     });
635:                 }
636:             }
637:         }
638: 
639:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
640:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
641:             self.walk_function_names(
642:                 child,
643:                 source,
644:                 diagnostics,
645:                 in_methods_block || is_methods,
646:             );
647:         }
648:     }
649: 
650:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
651:     // Statement validation (NOLHS, SEPEXR, REDEF)
652:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
653: 
654:     /// Check statements for issues (NOLHS, SEPEXR, REDEF).
655:     fn check_statements(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
656:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
657: 
658:         // Collect function names and variable assignments for REDEF.
659:         let mut function_names: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
660:         let mut variable_names: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
661:         let mut redef_reported: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
662: 
663:         self.walk_statements(
664:             root,
665:             source,
666:             &mut diagnostics,
667:             &mut function_names,
668:             &mut variable_names,
669:             &mut redef_reported,
670:         );
671: 
672:         diagnostics
673:     }
674: 
675:     /// Recursively walk statements for validation.
676:     fn walk_statements(
677:         &self,
678:         node: Node,
679:         source: &str,
680:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
681:         function_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
682:         variable_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
683:         redef_reported: &mut HashSet<String>,
684:     ) {
685:         let kind = node.kind();
686: 
687:         // NOLHS: Assignment with empty left side.
688:         if self.is_check_enabled("NOLHS") && kind == "assignment" {
689:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
690:                 let lhs_text = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
691:                 if lhs_text.trim().is_empty() {
692:                     let pos = node.start_position();
693:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
694:                         rule_id: "NOLHS",
695:                         message: "Assignment with empty left-hand side".to_string(),
696:                         severity: Severity::Error,
697:                         byte_range: node.byte_range(),
698:                         line: pos.row + 1,
699:                         column: pos.column + 1,
700:                         fix: None,
701:                     });
702:                 }
703:             }
704:         }
705: 
706:         // REDEF: Track function definitions and variable assignments.
707:         if kind == "function_definition" {
708:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
709:                 let name = source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()].to_string();
710:                 if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
711:                     && variable_names.contains(&name)
712:                     && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
713:                 {
714:                     let pos = name_node.start_position();
715:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
716:                         rule_id: "REDEF",
717:                         message: format!(
718:                             "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
719:                             name
720:                         ),
721:                         severity: Severity::Error,
722:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
723:                         line: pos.row + 1,
724:                         column: pos.column + 1,
725:                         fix: None,
726:                     });
727:                     redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
728:                 }
729:                 function_names.insert(name);
730:             }
731:         }
732: 
733:         if kind == "assignment" {
734:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
735:                 let lhs_kind = lhs.kind();
736:                 if lhs_kind == "identifier" {
737:                     let name = source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()].to_string();
738:                     if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
739:                         && function_names.contains(&name)
740:                         && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
741:                     {
742:                         let pos = lhs.start_position();
743:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
744:                             rule_id: "REDEF",
745:                             message: format!(
746:                                 "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
747:                                 name
748:                             ),
749:                             severity: Severity::Error,
750:                             byte_range: lhs.byte_range(),
751:                             line: pos.row + 1,
752:                             column: pos.column + 1,
753:                             fix: None,
754:                         });
755:                         redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
756:                     }
757:                     variable_names.insert(name);
758:                 }
759:             }
760:         }
761: 
762:         // SEPEXR: Missing separator between statements.
763:         // Check consecutive children of block/source_file that are statements
764:         // on the same line without separator.
765:         if self.is_check_enabled("SEPEXR") && (kind == "source_file" || kind == "block") {
766:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
767:             let children: Vec<Node> = node.children(&mut cursor).collect();
768: 
769:             for pair in children.windows(2) {
770:                 let prev = pair[0];
771:                 let curr = pair[1];
772: 
773:                 // Skip error nodes and comments.
774:                 if prev.is_error() || curr.is_error() {
775:                     continue;
776:                 }
777:                 if prev.kind() == "comment" || curr.kind() == "comment" {
778:                     continue;
779:                 }
780: 
781:                 // Check if they're on the same line with no separator.
782:                 let prev_end = prev.end_position();
783:                 let curr_start = curr.start_position();
784: 
785:                 if prev_end.row == curr_start.row {
786:                     // Check the text between them for a separator (; or ,).
787:                     let between_start = prev.end_byte();
788:                     let between_end = curr.start_byte();
789:                     if between_start < between_end {
790:                         let between = &source[between_start..between_end];
791:                         let has_separator =
792:                             between.contains(';') || between.contains(',');
793:                         if !has_separator {
794:                             let pos = curr.start_position();
795:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
796:                                 rule_id: "SEPEXR",
797:                                 message:
798:                                     "Missing semicolon or newline between statements"
799:                                         .to_string(),
800:                                 severity: Severity::Error,
801:                                 byte_range: curr.byte_range(),
802:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
803:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
804:                                 fix: Some(mlt_core::Fix::insert(between_start, ";")),
805:                             });
806:                         }
807:                     }
808:                 }
809:             }
810:         }
811: 
812:         // Recurse into children.
813:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
814:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
815:             self.walk_statements(
816:                 child,
817:                 source,
818:                 diagnostics,
819:                 function_names,
820:                 variable_names,
821:                 redef_reported,
822:             );
823:         }
824:     }
825: 
826:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
827:     // Helpers
828:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
829: 
830:     /// Find the last (rightmost, deepest) descendant node in a tree.
831:     fn last_descendant(node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
832:         let child_count = node.child_count();
833:         if child_count == 0 {
834:             return Some(node);
835:         }
836:         let last_child = node.child(child_count - 1)?;
837:         Self::last_descendant(last_child)
838:     }
839: }

841: impl Rule for SyntaxErrorsEngine {
842:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str {
843:         "SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE"
844:     }
845: 
846:     fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
847:         "Parser-level and semantic syntax validation"
848:     }
849: 
850:     fn severity(&self) -> Severity {
851:         Severity::Error
852:     }
853: 
854:     fn category(&self) -> Category {
855:         Category::SyntaxErrors
856:     }
857: 
858:     fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
859:         // File-level only — no node subscriptions.
860:         &[]
861:     }
862: 
863:     fn can_be_disabled(&self) -> bool {
864:         true
865:     }
866: 
867:     fn has_file_check(&self) -> bool {
868:         true
869:     }
870: 
871:     fn check_file(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
872:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
873:         let root = ctx.tree.root_node();
874:         let source = ctx.source;
875: 
876:         // 1. File name validation (BDFIL).
877:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_file_name(ctx));
878: 
879:         // 2. Collect skip ranges (comments and strings) for source scanning.
880:         let mut skip_ranges = Vec::new();
881:         Self::collect_skip_ranges(root, &mut skip_ranges);
882: 
883:         // 3. Source text scanning (BADNE, BADOT, TWOCM, BADCH, BADSP).
884:         diagnostics.extend(self.scan_source_text(source, &skip_ranges));
885: 
886:         // 4. Tree ERROR/MISSING node analysis (SYNER, NOPAR, ENDCT, EOFMI).
887:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_error_nodes(root, source));
888: 
889:         // 5. File structure validation (CLIS, CLTWO, SOFOC, SEMFU).
890:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_file_structure(root, source));
891: 
892:         // 6. Function name validation (FNDOT, FNSWA).
893:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_function_names(root, source));
894: 
895:         // 7. Statement validation (NOLHS, SEPEXR, REDEF).
896:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_statements(root, source));
897: 
898:         diagnostics
899:     }
900: }

2: //!

8: //! ## Checks
9: //!

11: //! |----|-------------|

13: //! | USENS | Variable used but might not be set in all code paths |
14: //! | PSET | Variable set in one branch but not others |
15: //! | SUSENS | Script variable used before set |
16: //! | SVNODEF | Variable in script might not be defined |
17: //! | STOUT | Output variable might not be assigned |
18: //!
19: //! ## Configuration
20: //!
21: //! ```toml
22: //! [lint.rules.UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE]
23: //! severity = "warning"

65: /// File-level rule engine that detects variables that might not be defined
66: /// before use. Emits diagnostics under multiple check IDs depending on context.
67: pub struct UnsetVariablesEngine {
68:     /// Rule-specific configuration (retained for future use / serialization).

74: impl UnsetVariablesEngine {
75:     /// Factory constructor — reads rule-specific params from config.
76:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
77:         let rule_config: UnsetVariablesConfig = config.rule_params("UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE");

98:     /// Run definite-assignment analysis on function scopes and emit diagnostics.
99:     fn check_function_scopes(
100:         &self,
101:         tree: &Tree,
102:         source: &str,
103:         symbol_table: &SymbolTable,
104:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
105:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
106: 
107:         for scope in &symbol_table.scopes {
108:             // Only process function-like scopes.
109:             if !matches!(
110:                 scope.kind,
111:                 ScopeKind::Function
112:                     | ScopeKind::LocalFunction
113:                     | ScopeKind::NestedFunction
114:                     | ScopeKind::Method
115:             ) {
116:                 continue;
117:             }
118: 
119:             // Find the corresponding function_definition node.
120:             let Some(func_node) = find_function_node_at(tree, &scope.byte_range) else {
121:                 continue;
122:             };
123: 
124:             // Run definite-assignment analysis.
125:             let da = analyze_definite_assignment(func_node, source);
126: 
127:             // Emit NODEF/USENS for possibly-unset variables.
128:             self.emit_possibly_unset_diagnostics(&da, &mut diagnostics);
129: 
130:             // Check output arguments: STOUT.
131:             self.check_output_args(scope, &da, &mut diagnostics);

137:     /// Emit diagnostics for possibly-unset variables from definite-assignment results.
138:     fn emit_possibly_unset_diagnostics(
139:         &self,
140:         da: &DefiniteAssignment,
141:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
142:     ) {
143:         // Track which variable names have already been reported to avoid duplicates.
144:         let mut reported: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
